BhanuDharma.name: Bhanu
BhanuDharma.note: One of ten daughters Daksha gave to Dharma (Yamaraja); her son Deva-rishabha fathered Indrasena. Not Bhanu, Krishna's son by Satyabhama. SB 6.6.2, 4-5

people.Lamba: Wife of Dharma; her son Vidyota generated every cloud in the sky. SB 6.6.4, 6
people.Kakud: Wife of Dharma; her son Sankata fathered Kikata. SB 6.6.4, 7

YamiDharma.name: Yami
YamiDharma.note: Wife of Dharma, one of Daksha's ten daughters given to him -- not Yami, Surya's own daughter and Yama's twin sister, the river Yamuna, already in this tree by a wholly different mother. Her son Svarga presides over the heaven that bears his name. SB 6.6.4, 7

people.Vishva: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Vishvadevas, the class of gods named for her. SB 6.6.4, 8
people.Sadhya: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Sadhyas, the class of gods named for her, old enough that the Rigveda already speaks of them as the gods before the gods. SB 6.6.4, 8
people.Marutvati: Wife of Dharma; her sons Marutvan and Jayanta are named for the storm-gods and for victory. Not the Jayanta already in this tree as Indra's own son. SB 6.6.4, 9

VasuDharma.name: Vasu
VasuDharma.note: Wife of Dharma, and the most consequential of Daksha's sixty daughters: her eight sons are the Vasus -- Drona, Prana, Dhruva, Arka, Agni, Dosha, Vastu and Vibhavasu in the Bhagavata's own naming (SB 6.6.10-11). The Mahabharata gives the same eight gods a different name each when they are born a second time, cursed, as Ganga's sons -- Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Aha, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha and Bhishma, already in this tree at Kurukshetra's era -- and only Dhruva's name survives both tellings. Not Vasu, Jamadagni's son. SB 6.6.4, 10-11

people.Muhurta: Wife of Dharma; mother of the Mauhurtikas, the minor gods who preside over the day's auspicious moments. SB 6.6.4, 9
people.Sankalpa: Wife of Dharma; her son, also named Sankalpa, is will and intention itself made a person. SB 6.6.4, 9
people.Patangi: One of Kashyapa's seventeen wives, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every bird. SB 6.6.2, 21-22
people.Yamini: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the locusts. SB 6.6.21-22
people.Kashtha: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every hoofed animal whose hoof does not split, the horse foremost among them. SB 6.6.29-31

SaramaKashyap.name: Sarama
SaramaKashyap.note: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the tigers, lions and other predatory beasts. Not Sarama the rakshasi who comforted Sita in captivity, already in this tree as Vibhishana's wife. SB 6.6.24-26

people.Timi: Wife of Kashyapa, a daughter of Daksha; mother of every creature that lives in water. SB 6.6.24-26
people.Svadha: Wife of Angiras, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the Pitrs, the ancestors to whom every shraddha offering is made. SB 6.6.2, 19

SatiAngirasa.name: Sati
SatiAngirasa.note: Wife of Angiras, a daughter of Daksha, and mother by him of the Atharvangirasa -- the fourth Veda, in verse form. Not the Sati of the Shiva story, another daughter of Daksha who shares only the name: a different wife, a different husband, and not in this tree, by the same decision that leaves Shiva out of it. SB 6.6.2, 19

ArcisKrishashva.name: Archis
ArcisKrishashva.note: Wife of the sage Krishashva, a daughter of Daksha; mother of the comet Dhumaketu. Not Archi, wife of Prithu -- a different woman the same word, arci ('flame'), also names. SB 6.6.2, 20

people.Dhishana: Wife of the sage Krishashva, a daughter of Daksha; mother of four sons -- Vedashira, Devala, Vayuna and Manu. Krishashva's first wife, Archis, mothered Dhumaketu alone; the text (SB 6.6.20) attributes each set of children to one wife, not both. SB 6.6.2, 20

DevaRishabha.name: Deva-rishabha
DevaRishabha.note: Son of Bhanu and Dharma; father of Indrasena. SB 6.6.5

Vidyota.note: Son of Lamba and Dharma; generated every cloud in the sky. SB 6.6.6

Sankata.note: Son of Kakud and Dharma; father of Kikata. SB 6.6.6

Svarga.note: Son of Yami and Dharma; presides over the heaven that bears his name. SB 6.6.6

Arthasiddhi.note: Son of Sadhya and Dharma, named among the Sadhyas; the rest of that class is left ungrouped, as Vishvadevas is for Vishva. SB 6.6.7

Marutvan.note: Son of Marutvati and Dharma, named for the storm-gods; the Bhagavata calls him and his brother Jayanta expansions of Vasudeva himself. SB 6.6.9

JayantaMarutvati.name: Jayanta
JayantaMarutvati.note: Son of Marutvati and Dharma, named for victory; the Bhagavata calls him and his brother Marutvan expansions of Vasudeva himself. Not the Jayanta already in this tree as Indra's own son. SB 6.6.9

SankalpaS.name: Sankalpa
SankalpaS.note: Son of Sankalpa and Dharma, sharing his mother's name: will and intention itself made a person twice over. SB 6.6.9

Indrasena.note: Son of Deva-rishabha, in Bhanu's line from Dharma. SB 6.6.5

Kikata.note: Son of Sankata, in Kakud's line from Dharma; his own descendants are called the Durgas, guardians of fortresses (durga is the word for fort) -- a class left ungrouped rather than named individually, and no relation to the goddess who shares the word. SB 6.6.6

Nandi.note: Son of Svarga, in Yami's line from Dharma. Not Nandi, Shiva's bull and gatekeeper -- an unrelated figure sharing only the name. SB 6.6.6

Dhumaketu.note: Son of Krishashva and Archis; the comet, an ill omen given a father and a name of his own. SB 6.6.20

Vedashira.note: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. SB 6.6.20

Devala.note: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. Not the sage Devala of the Mahabharata, a much later figure sharing only the name. SB 6.6.20

Vayuna.note: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana. SB 6.6.20

ManuKrishashva.name: Manu
ManuKrishashva.note: Son of Krishashva and Dhishana, sharing a common name ('the thinking one') rather than any connection to Svayambhuva or Vaivasvata Manu, both already in this tree. SB 6.6.20
